newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sees higher deficit, but to meet EMU target.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sees higher deficit, but to meet EMU target.

text.p: Germany's federal budget deficit is expected to surge to 70 billion marks this year, up from forecasts of 53.3 billion marks, but Bonn still believes it can qualify for European monetary union, government sources said on Friday.

The sources said that despite a higher federal budget deficit, Germany's total public deficits will still be restricted to three percent of gross domestic product, the limit set for monetary union in the Maastricht Treaty.

Government sources had said on Thursday that the level of the deficit would be higher than public investment, which is technically prohibited by the constitution except in certain extraordinary circumstances.

Germany is struggling to meet the fiscal criteria to qualify for Europe's single currency. Participants in EMU will be chosen next year based on their economic performance in 1997. The euro is planned to be launched in 1999.
